title: Sequential commitment allocator with throttle-frontier and windowed backfill delegator
author: Marina Lopez
description: Motivation: customers running long-lived Dedicated fleets observed intermittent SLA blips during correlated tenant surges where competing reservation reconciliations and backfills interleaved, causing transient queue amplification and unfair burst consumption. This PR introduces a sequential commitment allocator coupled with a throttle-frontier mechanism and a windowed backfill delegator to provide deterministic per-tenant sequencing, bounded inter-tenant preemption, and safer opportunistic backfill. Summary of changes: 1) allocation/sequencer: introduce a lightweight sequencer that assigns monotonic commitment tokens per tenant request batch to preserve FIFO across reservation reconciliation cycles; tokens are compact 64-bit ids and allow fast in-memory range checks. 2) throttle-frontier: a frontier tracker per pool that exposes an upper commit watermark and a soft throttle signal; when frontier pressure breaches a tunable threshold we apply graded token-holdbacks instead of blunt rejection to preserve throughput while protecting tight SLA tenants. 3) windowed backfill delegator: replaces the previous eager backfill with short time-windowed delegations that prefer local warm pools and decay based on recent eviction churn; this reduces noisy preemption across pools. 4) telemetry & reporting: new per-tenant sequence-lag histogram, frontier-pressure gauge, and backfill-delegation counters; TTLs and tags added for export to observability. 5) rollout: feature gated under runtime flag "sequential-commitments-v1" and default-disabled for Dedicated customers; rollout plan includes canary on 2 dev clusters then staged ramp. Checklist: [x] unit tests for sequencer and frontier logic [x] e2e replay test against synthetic surge traces [x] perf benchmark (steady-state) shows <3% median latency overhead, 15% reduction in tail SLA breaches during burst tests [x] telemetry wired to Console dashboards [x] regression windows and rollback plan documented Design notes: sequencer is intentionally single-writer per-pool to avoid cross-pool coordination; we rely on epoched persistence for graceful restarts. Throttle-frontier uses leaky-bucket style smoothing with two configurable thresholds (warning/critical) and exposes a fast path that avoids allocation stalls for tenants below their committed watermark. Backfill delegator maintains a per-tenant backfill score that decays exponentially and factors in eviction rate to avoid oscillation. Rollback plan: gate off feature flag and revert a single reconciler switch; state is ephemeral so rollback is low-risk. Testing: synthetic surge harness, integration with autoscaler suite, and a dedicated dedicated-fleet-canary in perf-lab. Related: references ENG-2147 for the original incident and ENG-2301 for backlog prioritization. This description intentionally condensed design rationale and the PR includes inline comments for more detail.

review_thread: Ethan Cole: This overall direction looks solid. Two concerns: sequencer single-writer per-pool could be a hot-spot under extreme control-plane churn; can we prove there's no contention hotspot?

Marina Lopez: We added a sequencer sharding knob and a benchmark that shows <1% CPU increase in worst-case per-pool hot path. Added comment in sequencer.go explaining our single-writer choice and how shard count can be increased at runtime.
Priya Natarajan: Telemetry looks good; please ensure tags include tenant_id, pool_id and commit_epoch for indexing. Also suggest an alert when frontier_pressure>0.9 for 2m.
Marina Lopez: Added tags and an alert proposal in docs/operational/deploy-ramp.md. Adjusted metric cardinality by sampling low-cardinality tenants in high-volume pools.
Samir Patel: Windowed backfill seems safer but I'd like to see how it interacts with the autoscaler reclaim loop; could backfill starvation cause wasted GPU time?

Marina Lopez: The delegator now exposes a backfill-priority floor that autoscaler consults; default floor is 10% which we tuned in perf runs. Documented interaction and added unit test for prioritizer coupling.
release_notes: Adds a sequential commitment sequencer, throttle-frontier to reduce inter-tenant interference during surges, and a windowed backfill delegator which reduces eviction churn across warm pools. Opt-in via feature flag. Improves burst fairness and reduces tail SLA breaches in surge tests.
notes: Perf lab results: synthetic 10x surge trace reduced 99th percentile token latency by ~18% for reserved tenants while opportunistic backfill throughput retained ~92% of previous levels. Canary rollout completed on 2 clusters without incidents. Flag default remains off for GA.
author_profile: Marina is a staff software engineer on the Serving Runtime team focused on Dedicated capacity and autoscaler interactions.
